correctness.rationale: Over a split nonmodular finite abelian group algebra, character orthogonality gives F_chi F_psi = N*[psi=chi^{-2}] F_{chi^{-1}}. The map chi->chi^{-2} permutes the odd-order character group and has no orbits of size 2; fixed characters are exactly the 3-torsion. The commutator coefficient map on each orbit is precisely a cyclic list of 2-by-2 determinants. A constructive lemma solves every prescribed cyclic list of length at least three, including zero and characteristic-two cases, and independent orbit solutions yield a single bracket for any vector in E_prime. Fixed-character coefficients vanish in every bracket and the nonfixed span is closed under multiplication. The accompanying self-contained checker tests cyclic determinant assignments and checks sample brackets against the original quandle multiplication, but the theorem follows from the paper proof, not those finite tests.

originality.rationale: The checked 2022 Section 7 and August 2026 Section 5 sources give bounds, small examples, and an open all-dihedral width question, but not the all-odd-abelian nonmodular splitting-field theorem. Zhang 2026 Theorem 2.3 ALREADY obtains the linear commutator subalgebra and its dimension via an augmentation/group-ring description; that subsidiary information is credited, not claimed. The new claim is nonlinear one-bracket surjectivity of every element of the existing commutator span. Direct published-finding corpus semantic searches of the claim, equivalent Fourier-orbit and commutator-width formulations and alias searches found adjacent quandle work but no source implying the full assertion. Broader implicit coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: An implicit single-commutator image theorem in general bilinear-map or Fourier-cyclic literature might subsume the result without matching quandle vocabulary.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed; the self-contained checker is diagnostic and finite.

value.rationale: The published commutator-width problem is motivated by understanding quandle algebra noncommutativity. This result solves an entire natural infinite class of odd-order finite abelian core quandles under transparent coefficient hypotheses, sharply classifies zero versus unit width, and provides constructive witnesses for arbitrary elements. The distinction between a known linear span and an actual single bilinear commutator cannot be reduced to a renaming or a one-line textbook deduction; the cycle determinant lemma provides the required nontrivial uniform step.
